# The operating system resolves a symbolic link before a ".." that
# follows it, so testdata/link/../input.txt names docs/input.txt,
# not p/testdata/input.txt. Check that a change to the file the test
# read invalidates the cache (go.dev/issue/82849).

[short] skip
[!symlink] skip
[GOOS:windows] skip 'Windows resolves .. before symbolic links'

env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache

mkdir docs/sub p/testdata
symlink p/testdata/link -> ../../docs/sub

# The go command refuses to cache access to files younger than 2s.
sleep 2s

go test -v ./p
stdout 'read: old'
! stdout '(cached)'
go test -v ./p
stdout '(cached)'

cp new.txt docs/input.txt
sleep 2s
go test -v ./p
stdout 'read: new'
! stdout '(cached)'
go test -v ./p
stdout 'read: new'
stdout '(cached)'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/dotdot

go 1.27
-- docs/input.txt --
old
-- new.txt --
new
-- p/p_test.go --
package p

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

func TestReadThroughLink(t *testing.T) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/link/../input.txt")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Logf("read: %s", b)
}
